title: Why the Ocean Isn't Where Most People Drown
titles: Why the Ocean Isn't Where Most People Drown
The Shocking Truth About Water Safety
Where Do Most Drownings Actually Happen?
hook: Most drownings don't happen in the ocean.

scenes.text: Most drownings don't happen in the ocean.
When thinking of water danger, we usually picture massive ocean waves.
In reality, only 10% of drownings take place in seawater.
Instead, an overwhelming 90% happen in freshwater like lakes and rivers.
People let their guard down around calm water, making freshwater far deadlier.
In fact, alcohol plays a role in roughly 50% of fatal drownings.
Even scarier, people have drowned in as little as 1.2 inches of water.
The deep sea feels terrifying, but local freshwater holds the real danger.
